newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London fall, led by banks.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London fall, led by banks.

text.p: Hong Kong shares in London were sharply lower on Thursday, hit by weak futures in Hong Kong, falling bank stocks in London and a weaker tone on both UK and U.S. stock markets.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index was down 77.82 points, or 0.65 percent, at 12,394.51 by 1510 GMT.
"The market opened weaker on the back of sliding futures in Hong Kong, which fell away as the market closed," said one trader.
"We recovered a bit on the back of bonds but now the (Wall) Street is going lower and we will continue in that vein."
Bank stocks helped set the weaker tone for the day after the sector was hit sharply in London.

"All the banks were knocked heavily in London this morning and Hong Kong bank was no exception," the trader said. "We have seen no follow-through buying, people are taking and holding profits in that sector."
HSBC Holdings was trading at HK$176.075 in London after closing at HK$177.5 in Hong Kong.
